modern: He often acts unjustly who does not do a certain thing; not only he who does a certain thing.
original: He often acts unjustly who does not do a certain thing; not only he who does a certain thing.
notification: He often acts unjustly who does not do a certain thing; not only he who does a certain thing.
notification_original: He often acts unjustly who does not do a certain thing; not only he who does a certain thing.

explained.summary: You can do wrong by failing to act, not only by acting. Standing by when you could help, or keeping quiet when you should speak, can be just as unjust as doing harm directly.
explained.today: Watching a colleague get blamed for your mistake and saying nothing, or seeing someone struggle with a pram on the stairs and looking at your phone instead, are both ways of doing wrong without lifting a finger.
